sentences.text: Facts, as pleaded in the application, which give rise to filing of the present bail application are that one person namely Himansh Kotwal made promise of marriage to the applicant and was in relationship for over a year, that under the pretext of false promise of marriage, the accused raped the applicant many times, more specific on 30 th March, 2025 as also on 1st April, 2025; that the accused reneged on his promise of marriage; that on 12.04.2025, the accused physically assaulted the applicant by injuring her right arm; that on the basis of the aforesaid complaint, FIR No.54/2025 stands registered at P/S Janipur against the accused for offences punishable under Sections 69/318(4)/115(2) BNS; that to the utter surprise of the applicant, she learnt that father of the accused, in order to escape from the criminal proceedings which were sought to be launched against them, lodged a false complaint against the applicant and the said complaint was culminated into lodging of an FIR being FIR No.58/2025 registered at P/S Janipur for commission of offences punishable under Sections 318(1)/352/351/308(6) BNS and the investigation got initiated against the applicant.
Apprehending imminent threat of arrest, the applicant has filed the present bail application before this court.

03. It is the case of the applicant that she, has been falsely and arbitrarily implicated in a false case foisted upon her, rather, it is the complainant's son, who physically assaulted and raped her many times on the pretext of false promise of marriage and in that regard, FIR No.54/2025 stands registered on 18.04.2025 at P/S Janipur against the accused for offences punishable under Sections 69/318(4)/115(2) BNS; that the complaint filed by the complainant is nothing but a counterblast to the complaint of the applicant.
Fearing threat of impending arrest, the applicant approached this court seeking grant of pre-arrest bail/anticipatory bail.
Pursuant to notice, objections, on behalf of the respondent no.1, stand filed.
However, perusal of order sheets reveals that respondent no.2 has not chosen to file his reply/objections.

A perusal of objections as also the status report filed on behalf of respondent No.1 would show that the investigation in the case is still going on as the statements of some independent material/key Steffy Gill vs The Union Territory Of Jammu & Kashmir on 25 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143799725/

Lastly, it is prayed that relief as prayed for by the applicant in this application be rejected.

06. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant has been implicated by the complainant, who happens to be father of the person namely Himesh Kotwal who had committed rape upon her under the false promise of marriage and against whom she had got registered a case on 18.04.2025, to settle score and harass her, so as to desist her to prosecute his son; that the criminal proceedings launched against the applicant are nothing but a device to harass the applicant, as such, she is entitled to be admitted to bail.

07. Learned counsel for the non-applicants argued and vehemently opposed the grant of bail in favour of the applicant stating that the applicant is in habit of implicating the innocent people and in this regard she has already threatened the whole of the family in implicating in false FIR and she has executed her threat on refusal to pay her the money; that, this court, however, vide order dated 30.04.2025 stayed the presentation of final report/challan.
Lastly, it was prayed that the application be rejected.
09. Hon'ble the Supreme Court, in a catena of judgments, has laid down principles for consideration for grant of anticipatory bail and how to exercise the power while granting bail.

In Bhadresh Bipinbhai Sheth Vs. State of Gujarat & Anr, reported as 2016(1) SCC(Crl) 240, relied by learned counsel for the petitioners, the Court while granting anticipatory bail for offence under Section 376 IPC has held:
"Before we proceed further, we would like to discuss the law relating to grant of anticipatory bail as has been developed through judicial interpretative process.

sentences.text: A judgment which needs to be pointed out is a Constitution Bench Judgment of this Court in the case of Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and Others v. State of Punjab [1980 2 SCC 565].

entities.text: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and Others v. State of Punjab [1980 2 SCC 565]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Constitution Bench in this case emphasized that provision of anticipatory bail enshrined in Section 438 of the Code is conceptualized under Article 21 of the Constitution which relates to personal liberty.
Therefore, such a provision calls for liberal interpretation of Section 438 of the Code in light of Article 21 of the Constitution.

The Code explains that an anticipatory bail is a pre-arrest legal process which directs that if the person in whose favour it is issued is thereafter arrested on the accusation in respect of which the direction is issued, he shall be released on bail.

The distinction between an ordinary order of bail and an order of anticipatory bail is that whereas the former is granted after arrest and therefore means release from the custody of the police, the latter is granted in anticipation of arrest and is therefore,
effective at the very moment of arrest.
A direction under Section 438 is therefore intended to confer conditional immunity from the 'touch' or confinement contemplated by Section 46 of the Code."

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Apex Court in case titled as "Ajwar Vs. Waseem & Anr"
connected with other cases reported as 2024 (6) Scale 461 in paragraph 26 held as under:
"26.

While considering as to whether bail ought to be granted in a matter involving a serious criminal offence, the Court must consider relevant factors like the nature of accusations made against the accused, the manner in which the crime is alleged to have been committed, the gravity of the offence, to role attributed to the accused, the criminal antecedents of the accused, the probability of tampering of the witnesses and repeating the offence, if the accused are released on bail, the likelihood of the accused being unavailable in the event bail is granted, the possibility of obstructing the proceedings and evading the courts of justice and overall desirability of releasing the accused on bail."
11.
The factual background of the case is that the applicant and son of the respondent No.2 had love affair and were in a relationship.
The non applicants have not pointed out the contravention of any of the conditions of the interim bail by the applicant herein after the grant of interim bail in his favour.
Without commenting upon the merits of the case, the matter for grant of bail in anticipation of arrest is to be considered.

12. Having regard to the decisions rendered by hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases referred above,
the allegations and objections filed by the Investigating Agency, lodging of FIRs by the parties against each other and considering the nature of the offences with which the applicant has been charged and also viewing that bail is the rule and jail is the exception, this Court is of the considered opinion that the applicant is entitled to be admitted to bail, particularly so when there are allegations and counter allegations which require full blown trial.
It will be in the interest of justice if the interim bail granted to the applicant is made absolute.

13. In the aforesaid backdrop of the matter, the law cited hereinabove and in view of the facts and circumstances of the case in hand, the bail application is allowed and the interim bail granted to the petitioner/applicant vide order dated 30.04.2025 is made absolute, subject to all the conditions therein.
14. The bail application is, 'disposed of' along with connected application(s).
(M A CHOWDHARY) JUDGE Jammu 25.02.2026
